scope: whole project (src/Leaderboard.tsx, src/TodoList.tsx; package.json and tsconfig.json read for context: React 18.3, strict true, no Next.js)

findings.title: 50k-row copy, sort and filter re-run on every keystroke
findings.explanation: The comment on line 5 states that `players` always holds about 50,000 rows. Every keystroke in the search input calls setQuery, which re-renders the component. Each render copies the array, sorts it (O(n log n)) and filters it, although the sort order depends only on `players` and not on `query`. This blocks the main thread on each keystroke, so typing in the search box can lag. The size comes from a code comment, not from a data source I could inspect.
findings.evidence:
const ranked = [...players].sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score);
  const visible = ranked.filter((p) => p.name.includes(query)).slice(0, 20);
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the sorted list once with useMemo keyed on `players` (const ranked = useMemo(() => [...players].sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score), [players])), and optionally memoize the filtered slice on [ranked, query]. Better still, sort on the server or when the data loads. If typing is still slow, use useDeferredValue for `query`.

findings.title: Array index used as key on removable rows that contain uncontrolled inputs
findings.explanation: Rows can be removed through onRemove, and each row holds an uncontrolled <input defaultValue={t.text}>. With key={i}, removing a middle todo makes React reuse the DOM nodes by position. The input keeps its old internal value, because defaultValue is only read on mount. After a removal, the remaining rows can show text that belongs to a different todo, and any text the user typed into an input stays attached to the wrong row. The aria-label also uses the index, so it is renumbered, which is acceptable.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the stable id as the key: <li key={t.id}>. Keep the index only for the aria-label.

limitations: Only two source files exist in the fixture; both were reviewed in full.
The 50,000-row size in src/Leaderboard.tsx is taken from a code comment; the data source was not available to confirm it.
Parent components and the real callers of Leaderboard and TodoList were not present, so render frequency from outside the components was not assessed.
No ESLint config was found; the tsconfig has strict true.
